openings.claim: Keeping retrieval with the evening clerk, movement-linked corrections to the existing exception slip may reduce second-location searches caused by stale entries. The proposed bounded probe is evaluated here; a daily intervention remains unproven.
openings.delta: For a small selected set of existing exception entries, the clerk crosses out and rewrites the location on the same paper slip whenever that book moves, retaining surname dividers and the existing shelves/cart.
openings.prediction: For selected books, recorded locations remain current through observed moves; pickups following corrected entries require fewer second-location searches than pickups following unchanged stale entries.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is household-surname misplacement: accurate location entries alone leave second searches concentrated among household-name mismatches, because the clerk consults the wrong surname region or entry.
openings.defeat: Selected entries remain accurate, yet second searches still occur because books are sought under another household surname; or the update procedure cannot fit the ten-minute preparation limit.
openings.probe: Within the existing preparation budget, capped at ten total clerk-minutes including any preparatory corrections, select as many exception entries as time permits and record household-name consistency and location on existing paper. During ordinary moves and pickups, the same clerk updates selected entries and uses the existing timing sheet to note second searches and durations. Keep all identity-bearing records behind the desk. If no time remains, select none; make no benefit claim from absent or sparse pickups.
assumptions: The synthetic eight-minute preparation sample does not guarantee spare time on another day.
Selected books may not move or be collected during the probe.
Sustainable update cost and attainment of the 95-percent two-minute target remain unknown; wrong-reader handoffs must still be excluded.
